guide.summary: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public unlisted app for your customers (app review); Public listed app in the Intercom App Store (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public listed app in the Intercom App Store (app review).

composio.note: Composio supplies a managed Intercom OAuth app, fine for prototypes. For launch, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret, and copy the redirect URL from the Composio dashboard into Intercom.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio's managed app works. For production, use your own Intercom public app so the consent screen shows your brand, you control scopes, and you get dedicated quota.
reasons: Managed consent screen shows Composio's name, not yours
Managed apps use Composio's default scopes and share quota across all Composio users
Intercom's review and listing apply to your own app

prerequisites.title: Free development workspace
prerequisites.detail: Public apps are built and tested in a free development workspace, which is for development only. OAuth is available in it automatically.

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace
prerequisites.detail: A private app for your own workspace needs a paid workspace. Some APIs also return 403 if the plan does not include them.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account or subscription, give Intercom test credentials or setup instructions in the app description.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register several, for example test and production.

steps.title: Tick Use OAuth in Developer Hub
steps.detail: In your development workspace, enable OAuth on the Authentication page and copy the client ID and secret from Basic Information.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list and justification
steps.detail: List only the scopes the agent really needs and write a justification for each. Canvas Kit apps get four scopes preselected.
steps.done_when: Each scope maps to a feature.

steps.title: Register Composio redirect URL
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it as an HTTPS redirect URL in Intercom.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom intercom auth config via Composio's API using your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Prepare demo script and test account
steps.detail: Draft a script covering OAuth install, full functionality and uninstall, plus test credentials for the description.

steps.title: Record the end-to-end video
steps.detail: Show install, features and uninstall, with the full client_id and state in the OAuth URL.

steps.title: Prepare listing and Partner Program pages
steps.detail: Provide company details, images in marketing format, a valid name and working installation links.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Fill in the Test and publish pages and click Submit for Review.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days; each resubmission can take the same.

steps.title: Set listing live in App Store
steps.detail: After approval, select List in App store on the listing page.
steps.done_when: App visible in the App Store.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes get rejected
traps.detail: This is the most common first-round rejection. Intercom may ask you to cut scopes and resubmit.

traps.title: Incomplete video means resubmission
traps.detail: The video must show OAuth install, uninstall and all functionality, with the full client_id and state.

traps.title: Changes after approval need re-approval
traps.detail: The live app keeps its current functionality until updates are approved, so plan scope changes ahead.

traps.title: Wrong regional host can fail
traps.detail: Intercom has US, EU and AU authorization hosts. For customers signing in with Google, the wrong host fails.

traps.title: Intercom in the app name
traps.detail: An app name containing Intercom will not be approved.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Consent screens show Composio's name, and quota is shared across Composio users.

blockers.what_it_means: Intercom found problems such as scopes beyond function, broken links or an incomplete video.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit; expect up to seven more business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Trim the scope list and check links and the video checklist.

blockers.what_it_means: The workspace's plan does not include that API.
blockers.what_to_do: Use a workspace on a plan that includes the API.

open_questions: Does a customer's workspace admin need to approve or install the app? Docs only mention the user approving; confirm with Intercom developer support or a test install.
Is there a minimum customer or install count, or a fee, for App Store listing? None found; check the App Partner Program page.
Real-world review duration beyond the 'up to seven business days' banner is not documented; ask Intercom developer support.
